overall_summary: Deduplication and temporal weighting of the provided dataset reveal a clear dominance of extreme space and 'What If' planetary scenario content published in late September and October 2026. Videos featuring hypothetical catastrophic planetary environments (e.g., liquid diamond planets, dark planets, burning ice worlds) and extreme cosmic phenomena (Venus's slow rotation, TrES-2b dark planet) achieve significantly higher view counts (800-1000+ views) and superior engagement (likes-per-view up to 0.037) compared to older, psychology or basic biology facts from early September.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (824 views) dramatically outperform standard biographical or biological facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes, sensory-rich 'What If' space exploration scenarios involving extreme planetary physics.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring bizarre physical traits of distant worlds like 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views) hook viewers effectively.
winning_patterns.action: Focus hooks on counter-intuitive space facts that violate common human intuition about time, light, and matter.

weak_patterns.pattern: Low-Stakes Human Psychology & Common Biology Facts
weak_patterns.evidence: Videos on memory creation, song psychological tricks, and standard animal facts (e.g., octopus hearts) generated significantly lower views (often under 100-200 views) and weaker engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological tricks and basic animal trivia unless framed inside a bizarre, high-concept narrative.
